name: Bacterial Spot
description: A bacterial disease that causes small, dark, water-soaked lesions on leaves, stems and fruit. It spreads fast in warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Small dark brown to black spots, often with a yellow halo
Spots may merge and the centre can fall out, giving a ragged look
Severe infection causes leaf drop and scabby fruit spots
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants
Avoid overhead watering and working in wet fields
Rotate with non-solanaceous crops for 2-3 years
Copper-based bactericides may help; consult a local agricultural officer

name: Early Blight
description: A common fungal disease that starts on older, lower leaves and moves upward, reducing yield if left untreated.
symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings (target-like pattern)
Yellowing of tissue around the spots
Lower leaves die first; stem and fruit lesions possible
causes: Fungus surviving in crop debris and soil
Warm, humid weather with alternating wet and dry periods
prevention: Remove and destroy infected leaves and plant debris
Rotate crops and avoid planting tomatoes in the same plot every year
Mulch to reduce soil splash; keep adequate plant spacing
Maintain balanced fertilisation; use recommended fungicides if needed

name: Late Blight
description: A fast-spreading and destructive disease that can destroy a crop within days in cool, wet conditions.
symptoms: Large, irregular, greasy-looking grey-green to brown patches
White fuzzy growth on the underside of leaves in humid conditions
Dark lesions on stems and firm brown rot on fruit
causes: Spores carried by wind and rain
Cool nights, high humidity and prolonged leaf wetness
Infected tubers or volunteer plants nearby
prevention: Plant resistant varieties where available
Improve air circulation and avoid wetting leaves
Remove and bag infected plants immediately
Apply protective fungicides on a schedule recommended locally

name: Leaf Mold
description: A fungal disease mainly affecting tomatoes grown in greenhouses or very humid conditions.
symptoms: Pale green or yellow spots on the upper leaf surface
Olive-green to brown velvety mold on the underside
Leaves curl, wither and drop
causes: Spores persisting on greenhouse structures and debris
prevention: Improve ventilation and reduce humidity
Space and prune plants for airflow
Water at the base of the plant
Use resistant varieties and sanitise tools and structures

name: Septoria Leaf Spot
description: A fungal disease producing many small spots on leaves, causing defoliation that exposes fruit to sunscald.
symptoms: Many small circular spots with dark borders and grey-white centres
Tiny black dots (fruiting bodies) in the spot centres
Lower leaves yellow and drop first
causes: Fungus overwintering on debris and weeds
Splashing water from rain or irrigation
prevention: Remove infected lower leaves and debris
Mulch and water at soil level
Rotate crops for at least 2 years
Control nightshade-family weeds; apply fungicide if recommended

name: Spider Mites (Two-Spotted)
description: Tiny sap-sucking mites that thrive in hot, dry weather and cause stippled, bronzed leaves.
symptoms: Fine yellow or white stippling on leaves
Fine webbing on the underside of leaves
Leaves turn bronze, dry out and drop in heavy infestations
causes: Overuse of broad-spectrum pesticides that kill natural predators
prevention: Inspect the undersides of leaves regularly
Spray leaves with water to dislodge mites; keep plants well watered
Encourage predatory mites and insects
Use miticides or insecticidal soap only as advised locally

name: Target Spot
description: A fungal disease causing target-like lesions on leaves, stems and fruit, favoured by warm humid weather.
symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings and a yellow margin
Spots enlarge and merge, causing leaf drop
Sunken dark lesions on fruit
prevention: Prune for airflow and avoid overhead irrigation
Remove crop debris after harvest
Rotate crops
Apply recommended fungicides if disease pressure is high

name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
description: A serious viral disease transmitted by whiteflies that stunts plants and heavily reduces yield. There is no cure once a plant is infected.
symptoms: Upward curling and yellowing of leaf margins
Small, crumpled leaves and stunted growth
Flower drop and very poor fruit set
causes: Whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) feeding on infected and then healthy plants
prevention: Control whiteflies with yellow sticky traps, nets and reflective mulch
Use virus-resistant or tolerant varieties
Remove and destroy infected plants early
Buy healthy transplants and control weeds

name: Tomato Mosaic Virus
description: A highly stable virus that spreads by contact and contaminated seed, causing mottled leaves and reduced yield.
symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic or mottled pattern on leaves
Distorted, narrow or fern-like leaves
Stunted growth and uneven fruit ripening
causes: Contaminated seed, tools, hands and clothing
Handling infected plants before healthy ones
prevention: Use certified virus-free seed
Wash hands and disinfect tools between plants
Do not smoke or use tobacco while handling plants
Remove infected plants and plant resistant varieties

name: Healthy
description: The leaf shows no visible signs of the disease categories this model was trained on.
symptoms: Uniform green colour
No spots, lesions, mold or curling
Normal leaf shape and texture
causes: Good growing conditions and plant care
prevention: Water at the base and avoid wetting foliage
Keep good spacing and airflow
Scout regularly and remove problem leaves early
Rotate crops and keep tools clean
